title: Renovation of the Fish Collection Facility on the Toutle River
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Portland District is hosting a two-hour virtual industry event at 0900 hours on 16 December 2026 to provide a project update and to gather industry input as it evaluates project construction risks, industry capabilities, and strategies for the project below. For those interested in seeing the project site in person, a site visit will be arranged for 15 December 2026. That site visit will start at 0900, and the site is located at 11285 Sprit Lake Hwy Toutle WA 98649. Firms who respond to this announcement with completed RSVP and Survey form will be provided further details for the site visit, if interested, and a link to the virtual meeting. The Government will provide the presentation slides following the event. It is also requested that each firm provide responses to a questionnaire to be launched at the conclusion of the event. Responses will be considered for use in the solicitation development.

title: Electrical Upgrades to the GCAFB/Tanker Base/Fire Cache
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial construction items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 127EAX27Q0015 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Electrical Upgrades to the Grant County Aeriel Fire Base and Tanker Cache on the Gila National Forest. This project consists of furnishing and installing a complete, code-compliant electrical distribution system to support a designated concrete pad area at the tanker base/fire cache, and the upgrade of an existing electrical/motor control panel serving the retardant pumping system. The completed system shall be suitable for continuous outdoor service in a high-use industrial environment and designed for durability, safety, and future expansion. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 238210. The small business size standard is $19M. This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency.

title: Primer Feed Mechanisms (PFMs)
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command - New Jersey, on behalf of the office of the Project Manager, Combat Ammunition Systems (PM CAS), intends to issue a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Primer Feed Mechanisms (PFMs) in support of the M777A2 155mm Howitzer. The PFM Assembly consists of three assemblies: (1) Body Assembly, (2) Tray Assembly, and (3) Magazine Assembly, and each assembly consists of several sub-assemblies. In addition to the PFM Assembly, the Dog Coupler Assembly (legacy), Reinforced Dog Coupler Assembly, Magazine Primer Stop, Injector Arm Assembly, Firing Pin, Cross Pin, and Inert Primers are considered down parts to the overarching PFM assemblies.Specifications: The contractor shall manufacture, test, and deliver Primer Feed Mechanism (PFM) assemblies and associated components for the M777A2 Lightweight 155mm Howitzer to support U.S. or Foreign Military Sales customers. Specific detailed packaging instructions will be included on the delivery order on a case-by-case basis.Planned Acquisition: The Government intends to award a single, five-year Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract with Firm Fixed Price (FFP) delivery orders with five one-year Ordering Periods (OPs) from Fiscal Year (FY) 27-32. The production contract award will be based upon Full and Open Competition as a 100% Small Business Set Aside, in accordance with FAR 19.5.The following Ordering Periods are anticipated:OP 1: 12 months from date of awardOP 2: 12 months from the end of OP 1OP 3: 12 months from the end of OP 2OP 4: 12 months from the end of OP 3OP 5: 12 months from the end of OP 4. **This Solicitation has been re-opened with Amendment 0006. Please refer to the Amendment for further information.**

title: Traumatic Brain Injury and Psychological Health Research Program Public Request for Information
description: The Congressionally Directed Medical Research Programs (CDMRP) seeks feedback to inform the fiscal year 2027 (FY27) Traumatic Brain Injury and Psychological Health Research Program (TBIPHRP) research focus areas and associated research funding opportunities. Although FY27 federal funds have not yet been appropriated, TBIPRP is collecting this information solely to support strategic program planning. This inquiry does not commit the program to incorporating this feedback into FY27 or any future TBIPHRP funding opportunities. The CDMRP wants to hear from all audiences, interested parties, and individuals from academia, industry, community and non-profit organizations, scientific and professional organizations, federal agencies, and the public. This RFI should not be construed as a solicitation or an obligation on the part of the TBIPHRP or the Department of War (DoW). BACKGROUND: The CDMRP represents a unique partnership between the U.S. Congress, the military, and the public to fund innovative and impactful medical research in targeted program areas. The CDMRP TBIPHRP�s vision is to optimize the prevention, assessment, and treatment of psychological health conditions and/or traumatic brain injuries. The TBIPHRP�s mission is to fund research to understand, prevent and treat psychological health conditions and/or traumatic brain injuries that accelerates solutions to improve the health and healthcare of Service Members, their Families, Veterans, and the American public. Appropriations for the TBIPHRP from FY21-24 and FY26 totaled $740.5 million. As of October 2026, FY27 funds for the TBIPHRP have not been appropriated. If appropriated, the CDMRP will utilize its two-tier review process https://cdmrp.health.mil/about/2tierRevProcess) to efficiently manage the TBIPHRP. Additional information about the TBIPHRP can be found here: https://cdmrp.health.mil/tbiphrp/ RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please provide responses to this RFI by clicking on the following link: https://www.surveymonkey.com/r/FY27-TBIPHRP-RFI

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE EPA REGION 1 - Superfund Technical Assessment & Response Team (START) 8(a) This is a SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE published for market research purposes. This is not an announcement for proposals, and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this announcement and any follow-up requests. The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 1, New England is conducting a Sources Sought, for informational purposes only, specifically to determine the availability of 8(a) small businesses and Alaska Native corporations under the 8(a) program capable of meeting the requirements of the attached draft statement of work (SOW). No telephone calls requesting a solicitation will be accepted or acknowledged. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. The requirement is currently being performed under the SBA 8(a) Business Development Program. EPA intends to retain the follow-on requirement within the 8(a) Program and is conducting market research to assess the availability of qualified 8(a) participants and determine the feasibility of conducting a competitive 8(a) acquisition. Interested firms must identify their current 8(a) Program participation status, applicable NAICS code, and relevant technical capabilities. title: Justice Command Center Phase II Renovation - RFI
description: Disclaimer: This notice is for informational purposes only. This is not a request for proposal or quote. It does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the government or a guarantee that one will be issued in the future. Responses in any form are not offers and the government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. No funds are available to pay for preparation of responses to this announcement. Any information submitted by respondents is strictly voluntary. The Department of Justice (Department or DOJ), Security and Emergency Planning Staff (SEPS) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to seek information regarding industry capabilities to provide modernization and enhancements to a 24/7 crisis management and communications center. Vendors should provide details on enhancing capabilities into a modern state-of-the-art facility suitable for executive level staff and their guests and increasing situational awareness capabilities. Vendors should also provide details on services they can provide for 24/7 operational centers. The DOJ is reviewing the marketplace to proactively examine all available options to ensure that the Department�s technology investments deliver maximum value, flexibility, and innovation today, and into the future. Project Name: Justice Command Center Phase II Renovation Background: The Justice Command Center (JCC) is a secure 24-hour facility operating in support of law enforcement and national security programs. The JCC is the primary information gathering and crisis management facility for the Attorney General (AG) and senior Department officials; it is designed to function during routine operations and emergencies. The last renovations to the JCC were in 2006 and consisted of minor cosmetic improvements. The JCC needs major renovations to continue to provide the best service possible to the Departmental leadership. Objectives: The Department of Justice Command Center modernization encompasses the renovation and upgrade of the JCC suite, which currently comprises three (3) conference rooms, one (1) watch floor, two (2) IT server rooms, two (2) restrooms, and one (1) storage room. The renovation shall deliver the following enhancements: upgrades to existing conference rooms to modern standards suitable for executive-level meetings and high-level briefings, modern design elements and finishes, renovation of the watch floor to support advanced situational awareness and real-time operational collaboration, and upgrades to all common areas and support spaces to contemporary standards while maintaining compliance with all security and operational requirements. Upon completion, the renovations shall provide a modern environment that is suitable for executive level staff and supports the JCC�s mission as the primary information gathering and crisis management center for senior Department officials. The JCC is a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF), therefore no devices with Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, photography, and/or recording capabilities are permitted within the JCC. 2. All visitors to the Restricted Area build site will be escorted/monitored by cleared personnel. title: Request for Information (RFI)- Parallel Battery Relay
description: 1. NOTICE This Request for Information (RFI) is issued for informational and market research purposes only in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. It does not constitute a solicitation, a Request for Proposal (RFP), or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. The Government will not reimburse any company or individual for expenses associated with preparing or submitting information in response to this RFI. The information provided may be used by the U.S. Air Force in developing its acquisition strategy, Statement of Work (SOW), and performance specifications. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary or competition-sensitive information. 2. BACKGROUND AND SCOPE The Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC), MH-139A Program Office (AFLCMC/WIH), is conducting market research to identify sources capable of providing Parallel Battery Relay modification for the MH-139A. The MH-139A missions routinely require off-station engine starts using only battery power. Flight data indicates that isolated battery starts in extreme cold weather degrade transient voltage, resulting in failed or hot engine starts. The objective of this effort is to modify the aircraft to parallel the main and auxiliary batteries during start sequences to prevent engine damage in austere environments. The Government considers Leonardo Service Bulletin SB 139-360 Rev C, Part II, (including Kit P/Ns 4G2430F00713) as the known baseline solution. Key requirements for the system include: System Functionality: Simultaneous utilization of main and auxiliary batteries during engine start sequences. Proposed solutions must either be the OEM kits or an equivalent FAA-approved modification that meets the exact same requirement. Airworthiness Support: The vendor must provide the necessary engineering data package to support a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) and a military Engineering Change Proposal (ECP). Critical Exclusion (Batteries): The USAF currently possesses compatible Nickle-Cadmium 44 Ah Main and 27 Ah Auxiliary batteries.[CA1] [BA2] [JC3] Modification pricing must strictly exclude the physical batteries and include only the installation hardware (relays, brackets, wiring, consumables). Support & Documentation: The vendor must provide the necessary technical data package (e.g., flight manual supplements, wiring diagrams, structural data, and software integration files) associated with their kit to allow the Government to integrate the modification into baseline aircraft and training devices. 3. INSTRUCTION TO POTENTIAL RESPONDENTS Respondents are encouraged to provide comprehensive responses that demonstrate existing capability, supply chain stability, and technical support qualifications. Please structure your response to address the following sections: A. Company Information: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, and Website URL. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Phone, Email). Business Size Status under NAICS Code 336413 (Aircraft Manufacturing), with a size standard of 1,500 employees. Please self-certify for all applicable categories: Small Business (Yes/No) Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) (Yes/No) HUBZone Certified (Yes/No) Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) (Yes/No) Company Ownership (Domestic or Foreign-owned). Interest as Prime Contractor or Subcontractor. B. Technical Capability, Logistics, and Sustainment: Provide a detailed description of your proposed hardware kit (whether providing the OEM baseline or an equivalent solution). Describe the Size, Weight, Power, Cooling, and Center of Gravity (CG) impacts of the installation hardware (excluding the batteries). Detail your strategy for interfacing the physical relay with the aircraft's Operational Flight Program (OFP) and Crew Alerting System (CAS) to provide pilot advisories, fault alerts, and engine Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC) interlocks.[JC4] If a physical switch or manual control is required for the activation of the proposed solution, the vendor must detail the strategy for aircraft modification, including the exact proposed placement of the interface to ensure in-flight aircrew accessibility. Provide engineering analysis or electrical modeling curves demonstrating the system's ability to maintain transient voltage above the engine hot-start threshold during a simulated start sequence at temperatures down to -40�C (-40�F). Provide proof of your company being part 145 certified. Sustainment & Tooling: Identify any proprietary or non-standard tooling required for installation. Identify strict shelf-life limitations or specialized storage/packing requirement for any kit consumables (e.g., adhesives, sealants). Confirm supply chain capability to provide individual replacement parts (relays, brackets) for long-term sustainment. Describe the technical data package provided with your kit and detail how your company will ensure the USAF Program Office receives future engineering revisions, safety notices, or updates related to this specific kit. Provide an impact analysis on how aircrew training syllabi and training devices (e.g., flight simulators, Weapons System Trainers, Cockpit Part Task Trainers, Operational Flight Trainers) will need to be updated. Acknowledge your ability to provide the necessary engineering artifacts required to support a Government CCB, ECP development, and TCTO generation. Facility Suitability: Describe the facility/depot where this installation would occur. Confirm that your facility meets the minimum footprint, tooling, and safety standards (e.g., specialized battery storage, hazardous material handling, and overhead clearance) required to perform the parallel battery kit installation. Throughput and Parallel Capacity: What is your maximum capacity for simultaneous (parallel) aircraft installations? Please detail how your facility layout and tooling availability support this throughput. C. Cost, Schedule, and Manpower: Provide a Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) cost estimate broken down in two parts: Non-Recurring Engineering (NRE): Electrical design, software/CAS integration, flight manual updates, and ECP/STC certification data package support, to include the engineering source data required for TCTO generation and Technical Order (TO) updates. Modification Kit & Field Installation: The per-aircraft cost to procure the physical hardware (excluding batteries) and perform the retrofit installation. Provide an estimated timeline for the development, testing, kit delivery lead times, and initial operational capability of the first modified aircraft. Validation of Maintenance Man-Hours (MMH): Respondents must name estimated MMH, and then clarify this estimate by addressing the following: The assumed environment/conditions for this estimate (e.g., controlled factory/depot environment vs. an operational flightline hangar). Active "touch-labor" hours vs. passive calendar/cure time, including whether the estimate assumes standard room-temperature or accelerated heat curing. Assumed crew size (single technician vs. multi-person). Inclusion or exclusion of post-installation testing and airworthiness sign-off time. Detail your available certified manpower (specifically avionics technicians and structural installers) to support the modification effort. Clarify if dedicated crews will be used for each aircraft, or if staff will be shared across multiple, parallel installation lines. Describe your crewing strategy for handling multiple, parallel aircraft modification lines (e.g., dedicated crews per aircraft vs. shared staff). D. Small Business Utilization: For Small Businesses: Describe how you will comply with FAR 52.219-14, Limitations on Subcontracting, if this requirement is set-aside. For Large Businesses: Provide a realistic small business utilization target as a percentage of total contract value and explain your rationale. 4. RESPONSES AND COMMUNICATIONS Responses shall not e

title: Germany – Special-purpose road passenger-transport services – Subvergabe Linienbündel Bad Mergentheim
description: Die Stadtverkehr Bad Mergentheim GmbH beabsichtigt als Inhaber der Genehmigung für den Betrieb des Linienbündels Bad Mergentheim nach einem neuen Konzept nach der Sektorenverordnung (SektVO) gemäß § 13 SektVO i. V. m. § 100 Abs. 1 Nr.1 und 102 Abs. 4 GWB mit Betriebsaufnahme zum 01.01.2028 zu vergeben. Der Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Neckar GmbH — B1 3-5, 68159 Mannheim — führt als Vergabestelle die Vergabe im Namen der Stadtverkehr Bad Mergentheim durch. Folgende Regelungen zur Tariftreue und Sozialstandards sind zur Sicherung der Betriebsqualität Teil der ausreichenden Verkehrsbedienung: Aufgrund der Arbeitsmarktsituation in der Metropolregion Rhein-Neckar und der Wirtschaftsregionen Vorderpfalz und Rheinhessen wird der künftige Betreiber verpflichtet, seinen Beschäftigten zur Sicherung einer aus-reichenden Qualifikation des Fahrpersonals bei der Ausführung der Leistung mindestens gemäß LTMG entsprechend der repräsentativ erklärten Tarifverträgen festgelegte Entgelt zu zahlen sowie die in diesen Tarifverträgen festgelegten Arbeitsbedingungen zu garantieren. Weitere Vorgaben finden Sie unter: https://www.landesrecht-bw.de/jportal/portal/page/bsbawueprod.psml/action/portlets.jw.MainAction? eventSubmit_doNavigate=searchInSubtreeTOC&showdoccase=1&doc.id=jlr- Tarift_MindLohnGBWpP8. Diese Verpflichtung gilt für die gesamte Laufzeit des neuen Vertragszeitraumes dynamisch, also stets mit Bezug auf die jeweils noch erfolgenden Anpassungen der Tarifverträge in der Zukunft. Erfolgt der Einsatz von Subunternehmern, haben diese ebenfalls die Einhaltung dieser Verpflichtungen zu garantieren. Zusätzlich zu den tarifvertraglich zu garantierenden Sozialstandards gelten für alle eingesetzten Fahrerinnen und Fahrer folgende Bedingungen zu Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen: Tarifvertraglich nicht als Arbeitszeit geltende Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen dürfen je Schichtmaximal 60 Minuten betragen. Überschreiten die Lenkzeitunterbrechungen und Pausen diese Grenze, sind die 60-Minuten-Grenze überschreitenden Zeiten der Arbeitsunterbrechungen der Arbeitszeit zuzurechnen. Als echte, nicht zu vergütende Freizeit im Sinne eines geteilten Dienstes zählt eine einmalige Arbeitsunterbrechung je Schicht von mind. 2 Std, die am Wohnort (Stadtteil) des Mitarbeiters oder an einem Betriebsstandort mit adäquaten Sozialräumen beginnen und enden. Die Vorhaltung von Sozialräumen ist in diesem Zusammenhang nicht relevant, sofern die Arbeitsunterbrechung länger als 4 Std dauert. Folgende Regelungen zur Personalübernahme sind ebenfalls zur Sicherung der Betriebsqualität Teil der ausreichenden Verkehrsbedienung: Die Bieter verpflichten sich im Rahmen ihres Angebotes, denjenigen Fahrer/innen einen Arbeitsvertrag anzubieten, die während der Vergabe im Betrieb des Altbetreibers des Linienbündels mindestens mit 70 % der regulären Arbeitszeit eingesetzt sind und die zum Zeitpunkt der Inbetriebnahme einen gültigen Arbeitsvertrag mit dem Altbetreiber vorweisen können. Der neue Arbeitsvertrag ist unbefristet und ohne Probezeit abzuschließen. Grundlage des Einstellungsangebotes müssen die im Unternehmen des Konzessionsnehmers für die übrige Belegschaft geltenden tarifvertraglichen und in Betriebsvereinbarungen geregelten Konditionen sein. Sofern der im übernehmenden Unternehmen praktizierte Tarifvertrag die Höhe des Entgeltes sowie die Zahl der Urlaubstage von der Dauer der Betriebszugehörigkeit abhängig gestaltet, muss der neue Anstellungsvertrag vorsehen, dass die Betriebszugehörigkeit beim Altbetreiber im Rahmen der entgeltlichen Eingruppierung und Urlaubsgewährung wie eine Betriebszugehörigkeit im übernehmenden Unternehmen gewertet wird.

title: Hochwasserschutz Gemeinde Wiesendangen: Fachmandat Architektur SIA-Phasen 32/33 und optional SIA-Phasen 41 - 53
description:
Die Gemeinde Wiesendangen ist wiederholt von Hochwasser des Wisenbachs, des Bachtobelgrabens sowie von Schäden durch Oberflächenabfluss betroffen. Insbesondere im Dorfzentrum bestehen aufgrund ungenügender Gerinnekapazitäten, zu kleiner Durchlässe und Brücken sowie historischer Hochwasserereignisse erhebliche Hochwasserrisiken. 


Für die sichere Ableitung eines HQ30 ist ein Teilausbau und die ökologische Aufwertung des Wisenbachs vorgesehen. Für den Schutz vor HQ100 wird das Wasser gezielt über die beidseitigen Dorfstrassen geführt. Mit Klappschotten, Kuppen, Mauern und Terrainanpassungen wird verhindert, dass es in Quartierstrassen, Gärten oder Gebäude gelangt. Ergänzend sollen Objektschutzmassnahmen die einzelnen Wohn- und Geschäftsgebäude schützen.


Das vorliegend ausgeschriebene Mandat umfasst die Planungsleistungen im Fachbereich Architektur für die SIA-Phasen 32 bis 53, wobei die Phasen 41 bis 53 als Option ausgeschrieben werden.


Wiesendangen ist gemäss dem Bundesinventar der schützenswerten Ortsbilder der Schweiz von nationaler Bedeutung (ISOS) ein seltenes und einzigartiges Beispiel eines Bachzeilendorfs im Kanton Zürich. Dabei werden die räumlichen und die architektonischen Qualitäten als sehr hoch eingeschätzt. Der Ortskern von Wiesendangen ist gleichzeitig im Inventar der schutzwürdigen Ortsbilder von überkommunaler Bedeutung enthalten.

Die Herausforderung aus architektonischer Sicht liegt primär darin, die Objektschutzmassnahmen in den historisch wertvollen und geschützten Ortskern von Wiesendangen so zu integrieren, dass sie einerseits den erforderlich Schutz vor Hochwasser gewährleisten und andererseits mit den Anforderungen des ISOS und des Denkmalschutzes vereinbar sind.

, les réaménagements des installations ainsi que tous les transports d’entrée et de sortie du chantier être effectués en dehors 


de la zone de circulation réservée au trafic de transit.  


La circulation à voie unique sera régulée par un système de feux tricolores commandé par radar. Aux heures de pointe


(y compris le week-end), une commande manuelle des feux tricolores par le prestataire 


doit être prévue si nécessaire. 


La longueur maximale du chantier est limitée à 300 m afin d’éviter des temps de dégagement trop longs.

title: UVT - Overscenemaskineri – Hovedsal, DKS-sal og Multirom
description: Stiftelsen Unge Viken Teater anskaffer komplett overscenemaskineri til Hovedsal, DKS-sal og Multirom i Kirkegata 11, 2000 Lillestrøm. Leveransen omfatter prosjektering, fabrikasjon, levering, montasje, styringssystemer, kabling for maskinfunksjoner, innregulering, prøving, dokumentasjon og opplæring. Hovedsal: 14 motoriserte trekk og 3 faste trekk, med nyttelast 300 daN (3,00 kN) per trekk. Motoriserte trekk skal holde og bevege scenisk last over personer som selvstendige maskinakser med hver sin last, UC3. Styresystemet skal støtte cues/scener og ivareta hovedleveransens UC3-bruk etter H-09. Tillatte driftsfunksjoner skal følge det tilkoblede maskineriets bruksområde. DKS-sal: 12 motortaljer à 500 kg og tre trosserammer à 7 000 × 2 500 mm. Multirom: 8 motortaljer à 500 kg og to trosserammer, 5 750 × 4 500 mm og 5 500 × 4 500 mm. Hver ramme løftes av fire taljer som koordinert gruppe for UC2. Heving og senking skjer med avsperret og tomt fareområde. Statisk lastholding over personer skal være dokumentert for maskineriets normale lastbærende system i alle salene. Opsjoner omfatter høyere brukskategorier, tre ekstra motoriserte trekk i Hovedsal, pantografer for kabelføring til alle tre trosserammer i DKS-sal og begge trosserammer i Multirom, samt ti flyttbare kabeltrommelenheter med 230 V énfase og Cat.5e til Hovedsalen. Opsjoner beskrives og prises separat etter O-01–O-08, inklusive kombinasjonstillegg O-01T og O-02T. Veiledende anslag for hovedleveransen inklusive fellesytelser: Hovedsal 2 000 000 kroner, DKS-sal 950 000 kroner og Multirom 700 000 kroner; samlet 3 650 000 kroner eks. mva. Tilbudet og opsjonene prises etter prisskjemaet. Det inngås én samlet varekontrakt etter NS 8407:2011 med tilpasningene i konkurransegrunnlaget. Tildeling skjer etter pris 35 %, kvalitet 35 % og klima og miljø – levetid og ressursbruk 30 %. Tidligste montasjestart er 01.02.2027. Hovedleveransen og utløste opsjoner O-01–O-05 og O-08 skal være ferdige og klare til overtakelse senest 31.03.2027. Pantografopsjonene O-06 og O-07 kan ettermonteres og skal være ferdige senest 30.06.2027. Prisevalueringen omfatter P-01–P-09 + O-06 + O-07 + O-08. Fullstendige krav fremgår av konkurransegrunnlag versjon 1.0, datert 11.11.2026, med kravbesvarelse, prisskjema og A20-01 revisjon 01.

title: Germany – Architectural and related services – Stadt Schrobenhausen | Stadthalle VgV-Verfahren mit Teilnahmewettbewerb nach §17 VgV und Lösungsvorschlägen nach § 76 Abs. 2 VgV
description: Im Rahmen eines EU-weiten Vergabeverfahrens mit Mehrfachbeauftragung von Lösungsansätzen soll eine belastbare Entscheidungsgrundlage für die künftige Entwicklung der Stadthalle in Schrobenhausen erarbeitet werden. Die unmittelbar neben dem Zentralen Omnibusbahnhof (ZOB) gelegene Stadthalle wurde im Jahr 1996 eröffnet und stellte über viele Jahre einen bedeutenden Veranstaltungsort für kulturelle, sportliche und gesellschaftliche Ereignisse dar. Aufgrund erheblicher brandschutztechnischer Defizite kann das Gebäude jedoch seit mehreren Jahren nicht mehr genutzt werden. Es liegen bereits erste Machbarkeitsstudien und Untersuchungen für eine Sanierung der bestehenden Halle wie auch Ersatzneubau vor. Die Stadt Schrobenhausen benötigt eine öffentliche Veranstaltungs- und Begegnungsstätte, mit einer Kapazität von ca. 470 (für Bestandssanierung) bis 600 Sitzplätzen (für Neubau). Aufgrund der bestehenden Förderkulissen und der zu betrachtenden Nachhaltigkeit ist eine Bestandssanierung zu betrachten. Eine Reduzierung der Sitzplatzkapazität um bis zu 130 Plätze kann daher in Betracht gezogen werden, sofern dies zur Ermöglichung bzw. Umsetzung der Sanierungsmaßnahmen erforderlich ist. Der Bereich um die Stadthalle soll in die aktuellen Planungen zu Landesgartenschau 2031 mit neuer Stadtterrasse und Zugang zur Paar integriert werden. Gegenstand der Aufgabenstellung sind realisierbare Lösungen für eine Bestandssanierung, mit Erweiterung oder Ersatzneubau der Stadthalle unter Berücksichtigung funktionaler, wirtschaftlicher und hochwasserschutzrechtlicher Anforderungen. Die Gesamtlösung soll eine langfristig tragfähige, funktional und gestalterisch hochwertige und wirtschaftlich umsetzbare Perspektive für die Stadthalle als Veranstaltungshalle mit Foyer, Gastrobereich (für den Betrieb den Betrieb während Veranstaltungen), Bühne und Funktionsräumen für den Veranstaltungsbetrieb inkl. teilbarer Saal, für Nebenräume aufzeigen. Die veranschlagten Gesamtkosten (KG 300-400) für die Baumaßnahme Stadthalle liegen bei ca. 9 Mio.€ Nettobaukosten. Die gesamten Kosten incl. MwSt. sollen bei max. 14,65 Mio.€ liegen.

title: Switzerland – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Gemeinde Oetwil am See, Beschaffung ICT-Betrieb und Infrastruktur
description: Die Gemeinde Oetwil am See will ihre gesamte ICT im Rahmen eines Full-Outsourcings an einen neuen Dienstleister übergeben, da der Vertrag mit dem aktuellen Partner Ende 2028 ausläuft. Die neue Lösung soll ab dem 1. Januar 2029 für alle sieben Standorte produktiv sein: Gemeindehaus, Altes Gemeindehaus, Werkhof/Wasserversorgung, Schulverwaltung, Schwimmbad, Feuerwehr und Bibliothek. Kern des Projekts ist die Migration der bestehenden Cloud-Umgebung in die künftige des Anbieters. Dort betreibt die Anbieterin Microsoft 365 mit Teams-Telefonie und SharePoint, die GEVER-Lösung GEVER365 sowie rund 25 Fachapplikationen. Zum Projekt gehört auch eine Netzwerkerneuerung im Mietmodell mit einheitlichem WLAN und Gäste-WLAN an allen Standorten. Weiter beschafft die Anbieterin 65 Arbeitsplatzinfrastrukturen mit Laptop, Docking-Station, zwei Monitoren und Peripherie und liefert sie fertig konfiguriert aus. Zu den einmaligen Projektleistungen zählen Projektmanagement, Datenmigration, Testphase, Rollback-Konzept, Dokumentation und Schulungen. Danach stellt die Anbieterin den laufenden Betrieb als Managed Service sicher, inklusive Client Management, Support ab 2nd-Level, Backup und verschlüsselter Kommunikation mit der Bevölkerung. Nicht Teil der Beschaffung sind die Gemeindefachlösung Innosolv, die Lizenzen der Fachapplikationen und die Druckerflotte.

title: Sweden – Building construction work – Ombyggnation Restadgård hus 1, 19 och 21
description: Migrationsverket är den myndighet i Sverige som prövar ansökningar från personer som vill bosätta sig i Sverige, komma på besök, arbeta eller studera i Sverige, söka skydd undan förföljelse eller ha svenskt medborgarskap. Migrationsverket erbjuder asylsökande boende och pengar till mat under den tiden de väntar på besked i asylärendet. När en asylsökande har fått sitt tillstånd att stanna i Sverige betalar Migrationsverket ut statlig ersättning till kommuner och regioner. Om en asylsökande får avslag på sin ansökan är Migrationsverket aktivt i arbetet med att få personen att lämna Sverige. Migrationsverket har boenden för asylsökande i egen regi. Migrationsverket har sitt säte i Norrköping, men har verksamhet över hela landet. Ytterligare information kan erhållas på vår hemsida www.migrationsverket.se (http://www.migrationsverket.se) Restad gård i Vänersborg är ett av Sveriges största asylboende. Migrationsverket har administrativ verksamhet på plats och det finns flera frivilligorganisationer som bedriver aktiviteter för våra boende. Entreprenaden omfattar att på totalentreprenad utföra ombyggnad av Hus 1, 19 och 21. I entreprenaden ingår nybyggnation av ett (1) stycken Miljöhus Laddning. Projektet ”Ombyggnation Restad gård, hus 1, 19 och 21” genomförs som en del av kraftsamlingsområde ”Sammanhållet mottagningssystem” genom EU:s migrations och asylpakt. Ett reformerat mottagningssystem där asylsökande vistas på mottagningscenter eller återvändandecenter ska bidra till att uppfylla regeringens mål om en effektivare asylprocess och ett effektivare återvändande.

title: Keyport Infrastructure Security Support Services Solicitation
description: *This Solicitation is for SEAPORT NXG MAC HOLDERS ONLY. No other offers will be considered. Seaport MAC Holders will need to register for PIEE accounts in order to submit offers.*Naval Undersea Warfare Center (NUWC) Division Keyport is soliciting a task order for Keyport Infrastructure Security Support Services (KISSS). This requirement supports the Infrastructure Services Division (Code 102) and the Security Division (Code 105).The scope of work includes, but is not limited to: Safety Compliance, Environmental Compliance, Facilities Engineering, Facilities Planning, Facilities Management, Facilities Maintenance, Security Operations Support, and Monitoring Support. The selected contractor will support Code 102 in its mission to plan, manage, and maintain NUWC Division Keyports safety, environmental, and facilities programs, while also providing security services under the direction of the Code 105 Security Office. The contemplated task order will be a Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) under the SeaPort NxG allowing any small business company in SeaPort to propose. It will be awarded on a best value basis to the Government. A trade-off analysis will be carried out, taking into consideration technical capability, past performance, and cost/price. The applicable PSC code for this requirement is R499 and the applicable NAICS code is 541330. The task order is predicted to be awarded in November 2027 with a predicted start date of January 2028. The support services are currently being performed under SeaPort-NxG task order N0025322F3001 by McLaughlin Research Corporation.

title: Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Multiple Award Task Order Contracts (MATOC) for Design-Build (DB) Construction in Support of Defense Health Agency (DHA)
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Little Rock District (CESWL) announces its intent to solicit for an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Multiple Award Task Order Contract (MATOC) for Design Build (DB) Construction Services in support of the Defense Health Agencys (DHA) Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) program.The Product Service Code is Z2DA (Repair or Alteration of Hospitals and Infirmaries), and the NAICS Code is 236220 (Commercial and Institutional Building Construction), with a size standard of $45 million.The scope of work for the resultant contracts will primarily be associated with the design, renovation/alteration of existing active medical facilities, but may also include major repair and new construction. Work may include restoration or modernization of hospitals, clinics, medical administration buildings, ambulatory health facilities, medical warehouses, medical labs, biological engineering labs, dental clinics, veterinary clinics, wellness centers, and any other buildings connected to or associated with the operations of Defense Health Agency (DHA) supported facilities. Required Contract Performance is within the continental United States (CONUS), Alaska and Hawaii (OCONUS), and US Territories with a potential for contracts to serve a certain region. The majority of work will be conducted in active healthcare facilities requiring multi-phase transitions of clinics and other operations. Experience and staffing for these types of projects is a requirement. Patient care and patient/staff safety in occupied space is paramount in design and construction. Compliance with all related governmental and non-governmental design and construction requirements is to be expected. Infection control in design and procedures during construction is paramount.Work may include, but is not limited to restoration and/or modernization of all aspects of heating ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration (HVAC-R) systems, plumbing systems, medical gas and vacuum systems, building envelope, roofing systems, anti-terrorism/force protection (ATFP) features, electrical systems, elevators, fire protection, interior renovations, wayfinding and signage, and exterior site and systems work such as utilities infrastructure, roadways, sidewalks, parking lots, landscaping, irrigation, etc. Work may also include providing transition services, and facility furniture, fixtures and equipment. Transition services include the planning and move of occupants, existing property, and associated services. Facility furniture, fixtures and equipment includes items such as casework, systems furniture, cubicle partitions, seating and desking, patient room furniture, artwork, and medical equipment.Under this contract the contractor must provide all necessary labor, material, supervision, and equipment for the design, construction, repair, and/or alteration to sustain, restore, and or modernize these facilities using Military Construction (MILCON) and Operations and Maintenance (O and M) processes. The contractor shall have experience in utilizing performance based requirements, where the customer identifies the objectives (desired result) and the constraints (code/criteria/standards) and the contractor is responsible for determining the means and methods to achieving the desired result. Any resultant contracts will be for a base period of five (5) years, with no option periods. Each contract awarded under the DB MATOC will share the total contract capacity estimated at $250 million over the five (5) year period. The estimated The minimum size of a task order awarded against this MATOC is $300,000, while the maximum size is $20M. Individual task orders will be competed among all MATOC base contract awardees. Firms must have ability to perform up to five (5) task orders simultaneously. The Government has a target of six (6) contractors.Small Businesses and 8(a) participants are reminded under FAR 52.219-14(e), Limitations on Subcontracting, that they will not pay more than 85 percent of the amount paid by the Government for contract performance, excluding the cost of materials, to subcontractors that are not similarly situated entities. Any work that a similarly situated entity further subcontracts will count towards the prime contractors 85 percent subcontract amount that cannot be exceeded.The acquisition will be advertised as a Total Small Business Set-Aside.The evaluation and selection of awardees for the MATOC will be conducted in accordance with FAR Part 15 ? Contracting by Negotiation, and FAR Part 36.3 - Two-Phase DB Selection Procedures. Awardees will be selected based on demonstrated technical competence and qualifications. A selection process will be used in accordance with FAR Part 15, Best Value trade-off Evaluation. The Government will evaluate performance capability in accordance with criteria described in the solicitation documents.The Government will post the solicitation and all subsequent amendments to the Government-Wide Point of Entry (GPE) System of Award Management (SAM) and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) Web Site http://www.sam.gov and www.piee.eb.mil. The offeror is solely responsible to obtain this solicitation and any subsequent amendments through these websites. Offerors are encouraged to visit the websites and become familiar with content and functionality prior to the solicitation issue date. Prospective Offerors must provide all information necessary to register for systems access and to receive posting notifications. Offerors must be registered and have an active, valid registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) database (https://www.sam.gov)and the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment Solicitation Module (PIEE). Offerors must also have a NIST Score recorded in PIEE to be eligible for award (https://piee.eb.mil/, to access SPRS/NIST Score). Anticipated solicitation issuance date is on or about 23 Dec 2024, and the estimated proposal due date will be on or about 05-Jan-2026. The proximity date of award is anticipated around 15-Jan-2027.

title: Sweden – Refuse disposal and treatment – Behandling av utsorterat matavfall 2027
description: Syfte Upphandlingens syfte är att säkerställa beställarnas behov av behandling av biologiskt lättnedbrytbart avfall under avtalstiden. En målsättning för beställarna är att upphandlingen ska bidra till minskad miljöbelastning inom avfallssektorn. Omfattning Med matavfall avses i detta kontrakt biologiskt nedbrytbart köks- och livsmedelsavfall enligt avfallsförordningen (2020:614). Anbudsgivaren ska hantera avfallet i enlighet med gällande krav på utsortering och separat insamling av bioavfall enligt avfallsförordningen och de fraktionsindelningar som där anges. Matavfallet ska hållas åtskilt från övriga bioavfallsfraktioner, exempelvis park- och trädgårdsavfall (exklusive fallfrukt), om inte annat överenskommits. Uppdraget omfattar mottagning, eventuell omlastning samt mellanlagring och biologisk behandling av biologiskt avfall, så kallat matavfall, från hushåll och verksamheter, pumpbart matavfall samt fallfrukt från hushåll insamlat från Nacka kommun, Värmdö kommun och Tyresö kommun. Den biologiska behandlingen ska bestå av rötning i rötningsanläggning för framställning av biogas och biogödsel. Biogödseln ska återföras till jordbruk/skogsbruk och ska vara certifierad enligt SPCR 120 Certifieringsregler för biogödsel, eller likvärdigt certifieringssystem, i den utgåva som gäller vid respektive tillfälle. I uppdraget ingår inte transport av matavfallet då transporten kommer att skötas av respektive beställares entreprenör, såvida inte behandlingsanläggningens placering kräver omlastning från respektive beställare.

title: Fiber Dial Room Refurbishment
description: INTRODUCTION Battelle Energy Alliance, LLC (BEA) Management & Operating Contractor of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) owned Idaho National Laboratory (INL), is seeking an Expression of Interest (EOI) from qualified vendors to provide refurbishment services for the Fiber Dial Room and implement point-to-point fiber connectivity upgrades. This initiative supports BEA�s commitment to maintaining robust and reliable communications infrastructure across INL facilities. BACKGROUND The Fiber Dial Room requires refurbishment and modernization to support enhanced fiber optic connectivity and point-to-point communication capabilities. The scope of work may include the following: Remove legacy abandoned communication cables around the plant. Refurbishment of several Fiber Dial Rooms around TAN, including structural and environmental improvements and replacement of hardware. Installation and testing of new fiber and communications. Installation and configuration of point-to-point fiber connections. Integration with existing network infrastructure and systems. Compliance with DOE cybersecurity, safety, and operational standards. Testing and documentation to ensure full functionality and reliability. INL is a U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) national laboratory dedicated to nuclear energy, national security, and clean energy innovation. INL is operated under a management and operating contract with the Department of Energy and as such, the Davis-Bacon Act applies for contracts in excess of $2,000 for the construction, alteration, or repair (including painting and decorating) of buildings or works at INL. Construction work at the laboratory Site covered under the Davis-Bacon Act is additionally subject to the INL Site Stabilization Agreement (SSA). These Site areas include all areas within the 890-square mile boundary, including the Material and Fuels Complex, Central Facilities Area, Advanced Test Reactor, Radioactive Waste Management Complex, and Specific Manufacturing Capability. The agreement is between signatory contractors and labor unions performing such work. Information regarding the INL Site Stabilization Agreement is available from the Site Labor Coordinator at (208) 524-4404 or at lance@sitelabor.org. Construction work performed at Idaho Falls facilities is not subject to these agreements. PROCESS This EOI is the first step in identifying interested and qualified vendors. Responses may be used to inform the development of a formal solicitation list. Selected vendors may be invited to participate in a Request for Proposal (RFP) process for award consideration. SUBMITTAL REQUIREMENTS Interested vendors should submit an Expression of Interest that includes the following: Company name and point of contact Description of relevant fiber installation and refurbishment capabilities and experience NAICS codes and business size classification Any existing DOE or federal contracting experience (if applicable) Deadline for submission: December 11, 2026 Submit to: Chase.Egbert@inl.gov Only select respondents, as determined by BEA, will receive an invitation to participate in the anticipated RFP solicitation. PROPRIETARY INFORMATION Because information received in response to this EOI may be business sensitive or proprietary to the responding party, respondents must mark information in their responses accordingly.

title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole-Source Contract for Large-Scale Additive Manufactured Temporary Radar Protective Covers
description: GENERAL INFORMATION AND STATUTORY AUTHORITY The Supervisor of Shipbuilding, Conversion, and Repair, USN, Bath, ME (SUPSHIP Bath) announces its intent to solicit, negotiate, and award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contract to the University of Maine Orono's Advanced Structures and Composites Center (ASCC), located in Orono, ME. The statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition is 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, "Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements." Pursuant to FAR 5.102 and FAR 6.305, the redacted Justification and Approval (J&A) document approved by the Competition Advocate (Code 400) on 4 September 2026 is attached to this special notice. 2. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT AND SCOPE The Government requires the design, material validation, physical testing, and fabrication of custom-fit, weather-tight, impact-resistant, and flame-retardant temporary protective covers. These specialized covers provide heavy industrial barrier protection for the sensitive, high-value AN/SPY-6(V)1 Air and Missile Defense Radar (AMDR) array faces on designated Flight III Guided-Missile Destroyer (DDG) platforms during active shipyard construction, outfitting, and pier-side integration. The anticipated scope of work comprises: Base Requirement (CLINs 0001 - 0004): Design review and engineering, material formulation and drop validation testing, and additive manufacturing delivery of one (1) initial shipset of four (4) customized temporary protective covers, including complete technical data deliverables under Government Purpose Rights (GPR). Support Services (CLIN 0005): Firm-Fixed-Price post-manufacturing support package consisting of pre-priced engineering hours for shipyard rigging coordination and fit-checks (SLIN 0005AA) and pre-priced field patch and repair material kits (SLIN 0005AB). Option Quantities (CLINs 0006 & 0007): Pre-priced contract options for up to two (2) additional replication shipsets of four (4) covers each (totaling eight (8) option covers) to support subsequent Flight III hull outfitting schedules. The total estimated value across the base requirement and all options is under $2,000,000, funded utilizing SCIB funding. 3. SOLE SOURCE JUSTIFICATION AND CONTRACTOR QUALIFICATIONS Detailed in the attached redacted Justification and Approval. 4. SUBMISSION OF CAPABILITY STATEMENTS THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. A solicitation will not be posted publicly. However, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. Interested parties must demonstrate in writing their existing, certified capability to meet the Government's technical and schedule requirements without causing unacceptable delays to ongoing naval construction. Submissions must include: Detailed evidence of an existing, fully operational large-scale additive manufacturing gantry system capable of printing a single-piece or modular thermoplastic enclosure matching the physical envelope of the AN/SPY-6(V)1 radar array foundations. Demonstrated technical capability to compound, print, and certify composite materials. Demonstrated ability to ingest shipbuilder 3D CAD parametric solid models directly into machine-ready additive instructions without requiring external mold tooling, and delivery of initial shipset articles. Company name, CAGE code, Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), business size classification under NAICS 326199, and primary technical point of contact. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future.

title: Design-Build Design-Bid-Build Multiple-Award Task-Order Contract in Lithuania and Latvia
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Europe District is planning a procurement to award a new Design-Build and Design-Bid-Build Multiple Award Task Order Contract (DB-DBB MATOC) for construction projects in Latvia and Lithuania. The MATOC will have a five-year ordering period with a maximum capacity of $49.5M shared amongst the awardees, and will expire at the end of the ordering period or when the maximum capacity is reached, whichever comes first. Note: Though the corresponding Sources Sought Notice (#W912GB27X1CPR) listed Estonia in addition to Lativa and Lithuania, the Government has opted to exclude Estonia from the MATOC footprint based on the results of market research conducted. The solicitation for this procurement will use the two-phase design-build procedures of FAR 36, FAR 16.5, FAR 15, and other regulations and supplements. The Government anticipates issuing a Phase 1 - Request for Qualifications in December of 2026, followed by a Phase 2- Request for Proposal in March of 2027 with a target of five awards in the third quarter of 2027. The Request for Qualifications will be posted here through the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) website. Interested offerors must be registered in PIEE to submit a response. Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification (CMMC) The scope included in the upcoming solicitation requires the contractor(s) and/or subcontractor(s) to process, store, or transmit Federal Contract Information (FCI) or Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) through their information system(s) and requires the contractor and/or subcontractor(s) to comply with CMMC requirements. For any task orders that follow the MATOC award, the CMMC level will be determined at the time of task order RFP. Cybersecurity compliance (NIST SP 800 / CMMC Level 1) is not reimbursable. Offerors must hold the required CMMC certification at the time of award and throughout task order performance. Proof of CMMC compliance is required to be uploaded to the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) module. The Government will use SPRS to verify certification status at award, and any offeror without the required certification at that time will be ineligible for award as their proposal will have failed to meet a material requirement of the solicitation and will be determined unacceptable. See DFARS 252.204-7021 "Contractor Compliance with the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements" and DFARS 252.204-7025 "Notice of Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements" for the definitions, requirements, reporting, and subcontract information for this contract/order/agreement. NATO Security Investment Programme (NSIP) Task orders awarded against this MATOC may be funded through the NSIP. Only firms from the 32 North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) countries will be permitted to participate as part of such task orders, to include the prime contractor, subcontractor(s), or manufacturer(s). None of the work required on NSIP-funded task orders, including labor and services, shall be performed by firms not registered and incorporated in one of the 32 NATO member nations. Additionally, no materials or items of equipment, to include identifiable sub-assemblies, shall be manufactured or assembled by a firm other than from within the 32 NATO member nations for such task orders. 1. Assembly: An item forming a portion of equipment that can be provisioned and replaced as an entity and which normally incorporates replaceable part of groups of parts. 2. Sub-Assembly: A portion of an assembly consisting of two or more parts that can be provisioned and replaced as an entity. 3. Manufactured: Made on an industrial scale. 4. Assembled: Fit together parts of. 5. Made in: Form from parts in. Note: The solicitation issued resulting from this notice will be in a separate announcement using the same Notice ID. A company must be registered and active in SAM to be considered for contract award. Further instructions and information can be found at https://sam.gov/content/entity-registration

title: Greece – Pest-control services – Ολοκληρωμένο Πρόγραμμα Καταπολέμησης Κουνουπιών στη Περιφέρεια Πελοποννήσου, για τα έτη 2027-2028
description: Αντικείμενο της σύμβασης είναι η παροχή υπηρεσιών καταπολέμησης κουνουπιών μέσω της εφαρμογής του συνόλου των απαιτούμενων δράσεων και ενεργειών παρακολούθησης και ελέγχου του πληθυσμού των εντόμων διαβιβαστών ασθενειών (προνυμφών και των ακμαίων κουνουπιών) στην Περιφέρεια Πελοποννήσου. Σκοπός του έργου είναι η προάσπιση της Δημόσιας Υγείας, η ποιοτική αναβάθμιση του επιπέδου ζωής των πολιτών και η προστασία του τουριστικού προϊόντος στη Περιφέρεια Πελοποννήσου, μέσω της άμβλυνσης των αρνητικών επιπτώσεων που προκαλούν τα κουνούπια. Οι παρεχόμενες υπηρεσίες κατατάσσονται στους ακόλουθους κωδικούς του Κοινού Λεξιλογίου δημοσίων συμβάσεων (CPV) : 90922000-6: «Υπηρεσίες καταπολέμησης επιβλαβών εντόμων». Η εκτιμώμενη αξία της σύμβασης ανέρχεται στο ποσό των δύο εκατομμυρίων τετρακοσίων δεκαεννέα χιλιάδων τριακοσίων πενήντα τεσσάρων ευρώ και ογδόντα τεσσάρων λεπτών (2.419.354,84€) μη συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ 24% ήτοι, τριών εκατομμυρίων ευρώ (3.000.000,00€ εκτιμώμενη αξία, συμπεριλαμβανομένου ΦΠΑ (580.645,16€). Η διάρκεια της σύμβασης ορίζεται σε 24 μήνες. Ως ημερομηνία έναρξης ισχύος νοείται η ανάρτηση της σύμβασης στο ΚΗΜΔΗΣ (αρ. 38 παρ. 7 του ν. 4412/2016). Αναλυτική περιγραφή του φυσικού και οικονομικού αντικειμένου της σύμβασης δίδεται στο ΠΑΡΑΡΤΗΜΑ Ι της παρούσας Διακήρυξης. Η σύμβαση θα ανατεθεί με το κριτήριο της πλέον συμφέρουσας από οικονομική άποψη προσφοράς, βάσει της βέλτιστης σχέσης ποιότητας – τιμής. Προσφορές υποβάλλονται για το σύνολο των υπηρεσιών του αντικειμένου. Η σύμβαση δεν υποδιαιρείται σε τμήματα λόγω της συμπληρωματικότητας και των αλληλεξαρτήσεων μεταξύ των υπηρεσιών που καθιστούν αναγκαία τη ανάληψη της συνολικής ευθύνης του επιχειρησιακού σχεδιασμού, της υλοποίησης και του αποτελέσματος του έργου.

title: Sources Sought - Modular Fiber Optic Test Platform
description: Issuing Office: 30th Contracting Squadron (30 CONS) Date Issued: 8 January 2026 Response Due Date: 12 December 2026, 3:00 PM PST 1.0 Description This is a Request for Information (RFI) for market research purposes only. 30 CONS is seeking to identify sources capable of providing a Modular Fiber Optic Test Platform that meets the salient characteristics listed below. The information provided in response to this RFI will be used to assess the marketplace and inform a potential future acquisition. This is not a solicitation for proposals, a request for quotations, or an invitation for bids. The Government will not award a contract based on this RFI, nor will it reimburse any costs associated with preparing or submitting a response. 2.0 Background Base Communications requires a portable and versatile test solution for the installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of fiber optic networks. The system must be modular to adapt to various testing requirements and rugged enough for field use. 3.0 Salient Characteristics Interested vendors must be able to provide a solution that meets the following minimum technical requirements: The system must be comprised of a modular mainframe and two (2) separate optical test modules as specified below. The mainframe must be battery-powered and provide a minimum of four (4) slots for test modules. The mainframe must have a minimum of 128 GB of internal flash memory. The mainframe must not contain any integrated Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or other RF-transmitting hardware. The system must include one (1) quad-wavelength OTDR module capable of testing at 850/1300 nm and 1310/1550 nm. The OTDR module must feature an intelligent link mapping capability that automatically interprets the fiber link and presents it as a simplified, icon-based schematic view with a pass/fail diagnosis for each detected event (e.g., splices, connectors). The system must include one (1) optical test module capable of measuring both Chromatic Dispersion (CD) and Polarization Mode Dispersion (PMD). All optical test ports on all included modules must feature a modular interface allowing for tool-free swapping of connector adapters. The system must be delivered with a fiber optic loopback mirror with a UPC polish connector. The complete system, including the mainframe and all modules, must be delivered in a single, hard-sided transit case. 4.0 Submission Instructions Interested parties are requested to submit a response electronically to Jeff Weeks at jeffrey.weeks.5@spaceforce.mil and Scott Yeaple at scott.yeaple@spaceforce.mil no later than 12 December 2026, 3:00 PM PST. Please ensure the subject line of your email reads: "Response to RFI FA461026SS0001 � Modular Fiber Optic Test Platform." Your response should include: Company Name and Address. Point of Contact (Name, Title, Email, and Phone Number). CAGE Code and UEI Number. Business Size (e.g., Small Business). A brief statement of capability (not to exceed 5 pages) detailing your ability to meet the salient characteristics listed in Section 3.0. Please include any relevant product datasheets. Please ensure the subject line of your email reads: "Response to RFI FA461026SS0001 � Modular Fiber Optic Test Platform." 5.0 Disclaimer This RFI does not constitute a commitment, implied or otherwise, that a procurement action will follow. All information received will be treated as public knowledge and will not be considered proprietary unless marked as such. The Government reserves the right to use the information provided to develop a future solicitation.

TECHNOLOGY LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: Multi-Channel Atomic Magnetometer (MCAM)
description: Unlike conventional multichannel atomic magnetometers that require one vapor cell and one optical system for each sensing channel, the patented Multi-Channel Atomic Magnetometer (MCAM) architecture from Los Alamos National Laboratory replaces many independent atomic magnetometers with a single shared vapor cell and optical system that simultaneously generates multiple independent sensing channels. MCAM is a non-cryogenic multi-channel optical quantum sensor in a single module that captures ultra-faint biomagnetic signals from the brain, heart and other sources with sensitivity approaching that of the cryogenic SQUID-based systems that have defined the field for decades. MCAM delivers that performance at roughly one-tenth the per-channel cost without a drop of liquid helium. The module pairs one large alkali-metal vapor cell with broad pump and probe laser beams read out by a photodiode array, providing 16 independent sensing channels in a single housing, scaling into helmet-style arrays of hundreds of channels, and flexing around the patient rather than forcing the patient into a fixed cryogenic dewar. Together, these attributes more easily allow for magnetoencephalography, magnetocardiography and magnetic-particle imaging while accelerating overall magnetic imaging workflows. Ongoing development is aimed at extending the sensing architecture from the centimeter scale characterized in the current prototype toward micrometer-scale spatial resolution, opening a path into cellular-scale magnetic imaging that current cryogenic and room-temperature arrays cannot address. How it Works The MCAM module operates on the spin-exchange relaxation-free (SERF) regime, in which atomic spins of alkali-metal atoms inside a large, sealed vapor cell are aligned by a circularly polarized broad pump laser beam through optical pumping and then interrogated by a linearly polarized broad probe beam propagating along a nearly parallel path. An external magnetic field of interest tilts the aligned atomic spins by an angle proportional to the field strength, and that tilt rotates the polarization plane of the probe beam through the Faraday effect; a photodiode array reads the optical rotation simultaneously at multiple points across the cell, with each photodiode pixel reporting on its own localized sensing volume. A buffer gas inside the cell restricts atomic motion so that the small cell volumes behind each pixel behave as independent sensing channels, a rear mirror folds the beams back through the cell to shorten the stand-off distance to the magnetic source, and transparent Pyrex wire heaters hold the cell at the operating temperature needed for SERF operation. Technology Description The patented shared-cell architecture generates multiple independent sensing channels from a single vapor cell, a single pump beam, a single probe beam, and a single detector array. A pair of broad, co-propagating laser beams, one for optical pumping and the other for probing, traverses the shared vapor cell to manipulate the internal atomic spins, converting the local magnetic field distribution into a spatially resolved optical signal that is read out by a multi-pixel photodetector. Because the buffer gas inside the cell restricts atomic diffusion, each pixel of the detector reports on its own small, spatially distinct region of the cell; therefore, the single module yields a two-dimensional map of the local magnetic field rather than a single-point measurement. Operation in the SERF regime, together with an integrated heating and shielding arrangement and a fold-back optical geometry that shortens the distance from the sensing volume to the magnetic source, sets the sensitivity floor in the low tens of femtotesla per root hertz at low frequency. A development path has been identified to reduce the effective sensing-volume scale from the roughly 1 cm per-channel footprint of the current prototype toward the 1 ?m range, which would extend the platform from whole-organ mapping into micro-scale magnetic imaging regimes. Architecturally, the MCAM module is engineered for arrays. Because all channels within a single module share one vapor cell, one laser pair, and one optics assembly, the per-channel parts count and tuning effort drop sharply versus designs that stack many single-channel sensors. Fiber-optic coupling between the laser sources and each sensor head lets modules be repositioned independently, so many modules can be tiled into a conformal helmet or surface array that adapts to head or torso shape and supports configurations that rigid large-cell predecessors cannot accommodate. The design is compatible with several alkali-metal and buffer-gas options and with per-module bias coils that allow each module to be tuned individually inside a larger array. Advantages Development path toward micrometer-scale spatial resolution, a roughly four-order-of-magnitude improvement over the current centimeter-scale prototype and an enabler of cellular-scale magnetic imaging Sensitivity at the low tens of femtotesla per root hertz, comparable to cryogenic SQUID arrays, while using a warm vapor, non-cryogenic architecture Roughly tenfold per-channel cost reduction by sharing one vapor cell, one laser pair and one optics set across 16 channels No liquid cryogens, eliminating recurring cryogen costs and simplifying siting, maintenance and shielding Fiber-coupled, repositionable sensor heads that conform to the patient rather than forcing the patient into a fixed dewar Scalable into helmet-style arrays of hundreds of channels, including a size-adjustable pediatric configuration Shorter sensor-to-source stand-off via rear-mirror beam folding, sharpening spatial resolution of biomagnetic sources Market Applications Medical Diagnostic Imaging (magnetoencephalography systems for epilepsy, stroke and neurodegenerative workups; title: Czechia – Construction work – Revitalizace sadu Svobody ve Zlíně
description: Předmětem veřejné zakázky je realizace stavebního záměru „Revitalizace sadu Svobody ve Zlíně“, která bude realizována souběžně a v úzké věcné, prostorové a časové vazbě na stavbu „Revitalizace zlínského zámku – I. etapa“. Stavba řeší komplexní obnovu veřejného parku a bezprostředního okolí nemovité kulturní památky Zlínského zámku, a to zejména v rozsahu nových zpevněných a mlatových ploch pro pěší a obslužnou dopravu, veřejného osvětlení, vodních prvků, závlahových systémů, krajinářských a sadových úprav, městského mobiliáře, slaboproudých technologií a souvisejících přeložek a přípojek inženýrských sítí. Stavba je rozdělena na část Park a část Okolí Zlínského zámku, přičemž obě části tvoří jeden funkční a provozní celek a budou realizovány ve vzájemné časové a technologické návaznosti. Součástí předmětu veřejné zakázky jsou rovněž terénní a sadové úpravy včetně následné pětileté péče o výsadbu a terénní úpravy. Plnění předmětu veřejné zakázky bude probíhat za provozu staveniště, sdíleného s dalšími stavebními záměry téhož zadavatele a s činnostmi třetích osob. Součástí plnění je následná péče o výsadbu v trvání 5 let od předání a převzetí stavební části díla Podrobnosti stanoví zadávací dokumentace, zveřejněná na profilu zadavatele

title: Udbud af rammeaftale vedrørende indkøb af træningsudstyr
description: Team Danmarks organisation består af en administrerende direktør, en sportsdirektør og ca. 50 medarbejdere, som arbejder inden for syv sportsfaglige områder: Sportsligt samarbejde, karriere- og talentudvikling, sportsmedicin, sportsfysiologi, analyse, ernæring og psykologi. Team Danmarks vision er at skabe de bedst mulige vilkår og rammer for dansk eliteidræt og for de enkelte atleter. At udvikle eliteidræt i verdensklasse handler således for Team Danmark om at sikre en rød tråd gennem atletens rejse – fra klubben, hvor det hele starter, hele vejen til toppen af medaljeskamlen og videre til livet efter sportskarrieren. Det handler både om mennesker og medaljer. For at kunne udleve denne vision er det afgørende, at Team Danmarks atleter og trænere har adgang til træningsudstyr af høj kvalitet, der understøtter optimal træning, restitution og præstation på højeste internationale niveau. Team Danmark ønsker således med dette udbud at indkøbe træningsudstyr, som netop skal bidrage til at sikre de danske eliteatleter de bedst mulige fysiske rammer og vilkår for at udvikle og udleve deres fulde potentiale inden for et samlet budget på 4 mio. kr. ekskl. moms. På denne baggrund udbyder Team Danmark en ikke eksklusiv kontrakt, der udbydes som rammeaftaler for en 4-årig periode, men hvor den leverandør, der tildeles kontrakten, er garanteret et engangsindkøb, der foretages af Team Danmark umiddelbart efter indgåelsen af kontrakten, og hvor det træningsudstyr, der omfattes af engangsindkøbet, skal leveres til Team Danmark senest i løbet af april 2027. Kontrakten vedrører et engangsindkøb af cardioudstyr samt løbende indkøb af cardioudstyr med et maksimumbeløb på i alt 2 mio. kr. ekskl. moms samt et engangsindkøb af træningsmaskiner samt løbende indkøb af træningsmaskiner med et maksimumbeløb på i alt 2 mio. kr. ekskl. moms. Det engangsindkøb, som Team Danmark forpligter sig til at foretage umiddelbart efter indgåelsen af kontrakten, er nærmere defineret i tilbudslisten. Udover engangsindkøbet har Team Danmark ikke aftagepligt på kontrakten. Det forventet indkøbsbehov over de næste fire år er indsat i tilbudslisten til brug for evalueringen. Dette forventede indkøbsbehov er alene vejledende og baseret på Team Danmarks skøn over det forventede indkøb og er således ikke bindende for Team Danmark. Dette betyder, at den leverandør, der tildeles kontrakten, ikke kan gøre krav gældende mod Team Danmark, hvis Team Danmarks indkøbsbehov viser sig at være mindre end det, der er anført i tilbudslisten. Ligeledes skal leverandøren kunne levere en større mængder, end hvad der fremgår af det estimerede indkøb, idet der i kontrakten er en bestemmelse om, at Team Danmark er berettiget til at forhøje kontraktens ramme med 50 % indtil seks måneder før kontraktens indkøbsperiodes udløb. Team Danmark har vurderet, at der ikke skal ske en opdeling af udbuddet i delkontrakter, jf. udbudslovens § 49. Baggrunden herfor er, at markedet for det udbudte træningsudstyr efter Team Danmarks vurdering rummer en række leverandører, der kan levere såvel cardioudstyr som træningsmaskiner, hvorfor en opdeling i delkontrakter ikke vurderes at være nødvendig for at sikre en bred og effektiv konkurrence om kontrakten. Hertil kommer, at en opdeling af udbuddet i flere delkontrakter ville medføre en uforholdsmæssig administrativ og økonomisk byrde for Team Danmark, herunder i form af koordinering af og tilsyn med flere selvstændige leverandørforhold, kontrakter og leverancer, hvilket ikke står i et rimeligt forhold til de fordele, en opdeling eventuelt kunne medføre. Kontrakten forventes at træde i kraft ved kontraktunderskrivelse og løber herefter i 48 måneder. De krav, der stilles til det træningsudstyr, der er omfattet kontrakten er nærmere beskrevet i kravsspecifikationen, der er vedlagt som en del af udbudsmaterialet. Tilbudsgiver skal stille en række vareprøver til rådighed for Team Danmark. De vareprøver, som tilbudsgiver skal stille til rådighed for Team Danmark, er markeret med grøn i tilbudslisten, der indgår som en del af det samlede udbudsmateriale. Udbuddet gennemføres elektronisk ved brug af udbudsportalen www.udbuddet.dk. Tilbudsgiver skal derfor oprettes som licenshaver hos www.udbuddet.dk. Oprettelse kan ske uden omkostning. Spørgsmål vedrørende www.udbuddet.dk skal stilles direkte til www.udbuddet.dk via support-funktionen, der kan træffes via telefon +45 7022 7007 Der ydes ikke vederlag for tilbudsgivernes deltagelse i udbudsprocessen. Hvis der nogetsteds i kravsspecifikationen eller udbudsmaterialet i øvrigt er henvist til standarder, skal enhver henvisning forstås som en henvisning til den nævnte standard eller tilsvarende. Opfylder tilbudsgiver ikke den nævnte standard, men tilsvarende, skal tilbudsgiver i tilbuddet dokumentere, at den tilbudte løsning på de relevante parametre er tilsvarende. I det tilfælde tilbudsgiverne fremsætter ønske om det, afholder Ordregiver gerne et infomøde forud for tilbudsfristen. Tilbudsgiverne opfordres i så fald til at tilkendegive ønsket herom på udbudsportalen.

title: Vesiliikuntakeskus AaltoAlvarin peruskorjauksen vaihe 4, pää- ja arkkitehtisuunnittelu
description: Vesiliikuntakeskus AaltoAlvarin peruskorjauksen vaihe 4, pää- ja arkkitehtisuunnittelu Jyväskylän Tilapalvelu pyytää tarjouksia Vesiliikuntakeskus AaltoAlvarin peruskorjauksen vaiheen 4 suunnittelupalveluista. Hankkeen eri suunnittelualat kilpailutetaan erillisinä hankintoina. Hankkeen kohteena on AaltoAlvarin vuonna 1955 valmistunut alkuperäinen uimahalliosa sekä siihen liittyviä vuosina 1964 ja 1975 valmistuneiden rakennusosien tiloja. Korjausalueeseen kuuluvat muun muassa 25 metrin allas, katsomo-, puku-, pesu-, sauna- ja teknisiä tiloja, kahvio- ja aulatiloja sekä vedenkäsittelyyn liittyviä tiloja. AaltoAlvari on Alvar Aallon suunnittelema kulttuurihistoriallisesti merkittävä ja suojeltu rakennuskokonaisuus. Rakennuksen vanhimmat osat kuuluvat UNESCO:n maailmanperintökohteeseen osana Jyväskylän yliopiston Aalto-kampusta ja Aalto Works -kokonaisuutta. Suojeluarvot ja rakennuksen ominaispiirteet tulee huomioida kaikissa suunnitteluratkaisuissa. Peruskorjauksen tavoitteena on rakennuksen teknisen käyttöiän jatkaminen sekä rakenteiden, tilojen, taloteknisten järjestelmien ja vedenkäsittelyjärjestelmien peruskorjaaminen ja uudistaminen. Suunnittelussa tulee lisäksi huomioida AaltoAlvarin toiminnan mahdollisimman laaja jatkuminen rakentamisen aikana sekä toteutuksen vaiheistus ja käyttökatkojen minimointi. Suunnittelutoimeksianto käsittää tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liiteasiakirjoissa määritellyssä laajuudessa hankesuunnittelun, yleis- ja toteutussuunnittelun, urakkalaskenta-aineiston laatimisen, rakentamisen aikaiset suunnittelutehtävät sekä vastaanotto- ja takuuajan suunnittelutehtävät. Hankesuunnittelun tavoitteena on tuottaa hankepäätöksen tekemiseen tarvittavat, eri suunnittelualojen kesken yhteensovitetut suunnitelmat, selvitykset, vaihtoehtovertailut, vaiheistusratkaisut ja kustannustiedot. Hyväksytty hankesuunnitelma muodostaa yleis- ja toteutussuunnittelun lähtökohdan. Hankkeen tavoiteaikataulu on: hankesuunnitelman hyväksyminen 10/2027 yleis- ja toteutussuunnittelu 2028 urakkalaskenta ja urakoitsijavalinnat 2028 rakentaminen 2029–2030 vaiheen 4 valmistuminen 7/2030. Hankesuunnitteluvaihe muodostaa itsenäisen vaihekokonaisuuden, jonka jälkeen tilaaja tekee erillisen päätöksen hankkeen jatkamisesta toteutussuunnitteluun. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tilaamaan toimeksiannon myöhempiä vaiheita, mikäli hankkeen toteuttamista koskevaa hankepäätöstä ei tehdä.,

description: Vesiliikuntakeskus AaltoAlvarin peruskorjauksen vaihe 4, vedenkäsittelysuunnittelu Jyväskylän Tilapalvelu pyytää tarjouksia Vesiliikuntakeskus AaltoAlvarin peruskorjauksen vaiheen 4 suunnittelupalveluista. Hankkeen eri suunnittelualat kilpailutetaan erillisinä hankintoina. Hankkeen kohteena on AaltoAlvarin vuonna 1955 valmistunut alkuperäinen uimahalliosa sekä siihen liittyviä vuosina 1964 ja 1975 valmistuneiden rakennusosien tiloja. Korjausalueeseen kuuluvat muun muassa 25 metrin allas, katsomo-, puku-, pesu-, sauna- ja teknisiä tiloja, kahvio- ja aulatiloja sekä vedenkäsittelyyn liittyviä tiloja. AaltoAlvari on Alvar Aallon suunnittelema kulttuurihistoriallisesti merkittävä ja suojeltu rakennuskokonaisuus. Rakennuksen vanhimmat osat kuuluvat UNESCO:n maailmanperintökohteeseen osana Jyväskylän yliopiston Aalto-kampusta ja Aalto Works -kokonaisuutta. Suojeluarvot ja rakennuksen ominaispiirteet tulee huomioida kaikissa suunnitteluratkaisuissa. Peruskorjauksen tavoitteena on rakennuksen teknisen käyttöiän jatkaminen sekä rakenteiden, tilojen, taloteknisten järjestelmien ja vedenkäsittelyjärjestelmien peruskorjaaminen ja uudistaminen. Suunnittelussa tulee lisäksi huomioida AaltoAlvarin toiminnan mahdollisimman laaja jatkuminen rakentamisen aikana sekä toteutuksen vaiheistus ja käyttökatkojen minimointi. Suunnittelutoimeksianto käsittää tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liiteasiakirjoissa määritellyssä laajuudessa hankesuunnittelun, yleis- ja toteutussuunnittelun, urakkalaskenta-aineiston laatimisen, rakentamisen aikaiset suunnittelutehtävät sekä vastaanotto- ja takuuajan suunnittelutehtävät. Hankesuunnittelun tavoitteena on tuottaa hankepäätöksen tekemiseen tarvittavat, eri suunnittelualojen kesken yhteensovitetut suunnitelmat, selvitykset, vaihtoehtovertailut, vaiheistusratkaisut ja kustannustiedot. Hyväksytty hankesuunnitelma muodostaa yleis- ja toteutussuunnittelun lähtökohdan. Hankkeen tavoiteaikataulu on: hankesuunnitelman hyväksyminen 10/2027 yleis- ja toteutussuunnittelu 2028 urakkalaskenta ja urakoitsijavalinnat 2028 rakentaminen 2029–2030 vaiheen 4 valmistuminen 7/2030. Hankesuunnitteluvaihe muodostaa itsenäisen vaihekokonaisuuden, jonka jälkeen tilaaja tekee erillisen päätöksen hankkeen jatkamisesta toteutussuunnitteluun. Tilaaja ei sitoudu tilaamaan toimeksiannon myöhempiä vaiheita, mikäli hankkeen toteuttamista koskevaa hankepäätöstä ei tehdä.,
